formulary_alternatives.therapeutic_notes: First-line substitute for most Amoxicillin indications. Cross-reactivity risk ~1-2% in documented penicillin allergy — elevated risk if anaphylaxis history.
Broader spectrum. Appropriate if penicillin/cephalosporin allergy confirmed. Check QT prolongation risk and CYP3A4 interactions (warfarin, statins).
Use if cephalosporin allergy or failure. Monitor QT interval and drug interactions.
Alternative macrolide substitute. Avoid in pregnancy and children under 8. Check photosensitivity risk.
Same drug, higher dose tablet. Can be split or dose adjusted. Confirm prescriber intent on dosing frequency.
Different mechanism. Use if metformin contraindicated (eGFR < 30) or not tolerated. Hypoglycemia risk — counsel patient.
Different class antihypertensive. Appropriate alternative for most hypertension indications. Not equivalent for heart failure — confirm indication with prescriber.
Same class as ACE inhibitor for most indications. Preferred if ACE inhibitor cough is a concern. Avoid in pregnancy — same contraindication as Lisinopril.
DOAC — different mechanism, no INR monitoring needed. Not a simple 1:1 substitute. Requires prescriber assessment of indication, renal function (CrCl), and bleeding risk. Escalate to prescriber.
Same drug class, equivalent efficacy for GERD and ulcer indications. Slightly different drug interaction profile — fewer CYP2C19 interactions than omeprazole.
Equivalent statin potency. Fewer CYP3A4 drug interactions than atorvastatin — preferred if patient is on macrolide antibiotics or other CYP3A4 inhibitors.
Appropriate for pain/fever without anti-inflammatory need. Use if NSAID contraindicated (renal impairment, GI risk, anticoagulant use). Different mechanism — no anti-inflammatory effect.
Different potency — dexamethasone 0.75mg equivalent to prednisolone 5mg. Requires dose conversion. Escalate to prescriber for dose confirmation before dispensing.
Same drug class, equivalent efficacy. Slightly higher QT prolongation risk than sertraline. Well-tolerated alternative.
Same drug class, equivalent bronchodilator effect. Slightly different dosing frequency. Appropriate direct substitute for mild-moderate asthma rescue.

drugs.dose_note: Half the standard dose. Suitable for mild infections or paediatric use. Confirm indication with prescriber.
Higher dose formulation for moderate-severe infections. Not interchangeable without prescriber confirmation of intended dosing frequency.
Starting dose for hypertension, or reduced dose for CKD/heart failure. Confirm prescriber intent.
Higher dose for inadequately controlled hypertension. Not interchangeable without prescriber confirmation.
Maintenance or higher therapeutic dose. Confirm prescriber intent before substituting.
Starting dose for sensitive patients or elderly. Not a direct substitute without prescriber confirmation.

formulary_alternatives.therapeutic_notes: Same macrolide class. First-line alternative when erythromycin unavailable. Better GI tolerability. Monitor QT interval.
Non-selective beta blocker with alpha-blocking activity. Preferred in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
Same ARB class. Well-tolerated alternative with comparable antihypertensive efficacy.
Same ACE inhibitor class. Equivalent blood pressure and cardioprotective efficacy.
Alternative sulfonylurea. Shorter duration of action — lower hypoglycemia risk in elderly or renally impaired patients.
Same NSAID class. Equivalent for mild-to-moderate pain. Avoid in patients with GI bleed history, renal impairment, or aspirin allergy.
Alternative opioid analgesic for moderate pain. Tramadol has serotonergic activity — avoid with SSRIs/SNRIs.
Same active drug, inhaler formulation. Currently out of stock — use nebuliser solution instead.
Shorter-acting benzodiazepine. Preferred in elderly patients and those with hepatic impairment — no active metabolites.
Atypical antipsychotic — lower extrapyramidal side effect risk than haloperidol. Monitor QT interval and metabolic effects.
SSRI preferred over TCA for most depression — better tolerability and safer in overdose. TCA may be retained for neuropathic pain indications.
Alternative corticosteroid. Note very low stock — consider ordering replenishment.
